feedback: This is the first candidate, so there is no earlier race outcome or Evaluator Race Data to cite. The review rests on the public contract. Every field is inside its stated range: five sensors at x = -0.04 to 0.04 with y = 0.04 (within -0.06 to 0.08), sensor_size 0.012, and wheel_track, wheel_radius, body_width, body_length and mass all in range. sensor_weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2) match the sensor order, so a positive signal steers left as the contract requires. line_loss 'last_direction' is a valid option. The candidate is valid and not obviously broken, which is the bar when nothing has raced. The stated speed target (about 1.5 m/s average) is an assumption from the contract's 3 s limit, not a measured value, so the main unknowns are whether base_speed 1.6 keeps the robot on the line through the tighter bends and whether kp=3 with kd=0.15 oscillates. Read the race telemetry before choosing the next change. If the run does not complete because it is too slow, raise base_speed. If it leaves the track or shows line-loss events on the sharpest bend, lower base_speed or raise kd. If it completes with high steering_oscillation, raise kd before changing kp. Keep sensor geometry fixed for this first race so its result can be attributed to the controller.
requested_changes: If the next race does not complete or progress stalls below full coverage, raise controller.base_speed (for example to 1.8) and keep the other fields as they are, so speed is the only variable.
If steering_oscillation is high or the robot drifts on the slalom, raise controller.kd (for example from 0.15 to 0.3) before changing kp, which the contract scales by 350 PWM per unit of turn.
If line_loss_events is above zero, test controller.line_loss 'search_right' or 'search_left' only as a comparison, and keep the same kp, ki and kd so the change in line-loss count is attributable.
